question: Which of the following chemical equations is INCORRECT?
solution:
The correct answer is __**CO(g) + H2(g) → CH2**____**O (l)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**CO(g) + H₂(g) → CH₂O(l): This reaction is not feasible as written.

 
• Typically, the synthesis of formaldehyde (CH₂O) from carbon monoxide (CO) and hydrogen (H₂) does not proceed directly in this manner.
 
• Instead, formaldehyde is generally produced industrially by the oxidation of methanol or by processes involving careful control of conditions, which do not simply involve the direct combination of CO and H₂.
